dialog.body: Zoning and Inspections, this is Greg.
Hello, good morning. Yes, my name is Luis Castillo. I am calling, um, because I have a question about the fence. Or the pool. Is both, really.
Okay, Mr. Castillo, take your time. Which one are you doing, a fence or a pool?

A pool. I am building a pool in the back, no, my landlord, he is okay with it, he say yes. And I read somewhere is a barrier you need around the pool. A barrier, a fence, I don't know the word exactly. So I want to know the rules for this barrier.
Gotcha. Yeah, pools generally have to have a barrier around them, a fence or a wall, with a gate that closes and latches. What kind of fence are you thinking about?
I am thinking composite. The plastic-wood, you know? Not the wood real. And four feet tall. Four feet is okay?

Four feet might be on the short side for a pool barrier. I don't want to say a number off the top of my head, but the pool rules are usually stricter than a regular backyard fence. We'd check that when you apply.
Apply. So, wait. I need to apply? That is my question, really. A fence, it needs a permit, yes or no? Because my nephew, he say no, you just build it. But the neighbor, she say yes, you need paper.
Both of them have a piece of it. For a regular fence, it depends on the height and where it goes. But for a pool barrier, yes, you're going to need a permit. And the pool itself will need one too.
The pool too? Two permits? One for the pool and one for the fence?
Usually it gets handled together, but yeah, the pool and the barrier both get reviewed. Is this an in-ground pool or an above-ground one?

Hmm. [pause] Sorry, one second, I am looking for the remote, the television is very loud, it is in the, how you say, the cushions of the couch. [pause] Okay, I find it. Sorry. Above ground. The kind with the wall, the, the metal wall, and the ladder.
No problem. Okay, above-ground. Those can still need a barrier, depending on the wall height and whether the ladder comes off. That's something the inspector will go over with you.
The ladder comes off, yes. So then is no barrier? I don't understand. You say yes the barrier, now you say maybe no.

Fair, I'm confusing you. Let me say it simple. Don't buy or build anything yet. Apply for the permit first, and the review will tell you if the pool wall counts as the barrier or if you need the fence too.
Okay, okay. Apply first. And another thing. How close to the line of the property I can put the fence? Like, to the neighbor? I want to put it near the edge, so I have more space for the pool.

There's usually a setback for structures and the fence has its own rules, and I can't give you the exact distance from memory. What I'd tell you is don't assume you can go right up to the line. Bring a plan showing where the pool and fence go and the distance to the property line.
A plan. I draw it myself? On paper?
A simple drawing is fine. Show the house, the pool, the fence, and measurements. If you have a survey from the landlord, even better.
Survey, ah, I don't have. The landlord, maybe he has. I ask him. And the permit, I can come to City Hall for the paper?
Yep, come by the office and we'll give you the application. Or the landlord can get it started, since he's the owner. He may have to sign anyway.

He has to sign. Okay. So, I tell you if I understand. First I talk to the landlord for the survey. Then I draw the plan. Then I come with the plan, and I apply for the pool and the fence together. And the fence, composite four feet, we see if is okay.
That's it, you've got it. Just one correction, don't plan on four feet as final. Let the review tell you.
Okay, not final. Four feet maybe more. Is the address 55 Callender Avenue, the North End. Do you need that now?
Good, I've got that written down. Bring it with you when you come in. We're open till four-thirty today.
Today is Friday, yes? Then I go maybe today, if the landlord is home. If not, Monday.
Either works. Monday's fine.
Okay. Thank you very much, Greg. I am still little bit mixed up, but I think with the paper it will be more clear.
That's normal. Ask the counter folks when you're in and they'll walk you through it. Take care, Mr. Castillo.
Thank you. Goodbye.
